In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have not detected any UHE neutrinos, and that we have not yet reached our sensitivity goal of one neutrino event per year, but we have demonstrated that the LUNASKA technique is feasible with current technology and that we have the potential to achieve this goal in the future.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have achieved the first detection of lunar Cherenkov emission from a radio-telescope array, but that the sensitivity of our observations is limited by the low signal-to-noise ratio of our current observations.

the lunar Cherenko technique has been demonstrated to work with the ATCA and the next step would be to use all six antennas, which would allow us to use a much larger bandwidth and hence to increase our sensitivity by a factor of about 10.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated that we can detect and characterise lunar Cherenkov pulses with ATCA and that the lunar Cherenkor technique is a viable technique for the SKA.
we have demonstrated the ability to make sensitive lunar Cherenkov observations using the current ATCA array.
